Table Tools

Copy these sheets or keep equivalent notes. Use only the fields that help you run the current session. A short record you can find is more useful than a complete history nobody has time to read.

Session preparation

PromptNotes
What the heroes intend next
Opening situation and visible stakes
Three people likely to matter
Useful locations and routes
Essential clues and independent ways to find them
Potential opponents and creature-card links
What changes if nobody intervenes
Rewards and their actual owners
Unresolved promises or consequences from last session

Encounter record

Before playNotes
Party: names, levels, cards and relevant defenses
Current HP, Grit, wounds and important supplies
Heroes' objective; opposition's objective
Initial budget and difficulty intention
Roster, individual CVs and total, including possible waves
Map: entries, exits, cover, terrain and hazards
Signs, information and counterplay available
Retreat or surrender circumstances
After playNotes
Rounds and how the encounter ended
HP loss; healing actions and caster HP costs
Grit spent; new wounds; deaths or Last Words
Supplies depleted or equipment lost
Disabled turns and important movement effects
Counterplay discovered and used
Choices the players enjoyed; moments of confusion
One change to examine before the next test

NPC and faction record

PromptNotes
Name and recognizable detail
Wants now
Knows or wrongly believes
Can offer; fears losing
Boundary or reason to compromise
Relevant people and loyalties
What they actually learned about the heroes
Next action if left alone

Location record

PromptNotes
Name, original purpose and present use
Two or three arrival details
Entrances, exits and alternate routes
Inhabitants and their reasons to be here
Discoveries and ordinary ways to reveal them
Hazards: signs, trigger, resolution and counterplay
Treasure, ownership and access
What the heroes changed

Recovery record

HeroPrior scarsCurrent wound/table resultLasting effectTreatment / RVProgressLast attempt day

Keep Grit expenditure and grants separately from treatment. Completing treatment removes the listed effect, not the scar. A wound receives at most one treatment attempt per day across every healer who could treat it.

Turn and outcome reminder

MomentCheck
Combat beginsOne unmodified 3d6: 12+ players start, otherwise opposition. That side starts every round.
Choose next actorAlternate sides; each chooses an unacted member. Finish the remaining side when the other has none.
Start of affected turnChoose retained categories for Dazed/Grappled. If Dying, choose Grit or death roll.
Before rollingDeclare card, target, action, applicable Boons/Banes and consequences.
Provoking action startsAvailable opportunity Reaction resolves Basic Melee first; continue if capable.
Resolve attackCorrect attacker/defender perspective; full outcome, weakness then resistance; minimum 1 per damaging event.
End of turnResolve temporary condition effects, then decrease their ratings by 1. Use printed expiries for other effects.
Danger endsResolve Dying and immediate hazards; take a safe breath when possible. HP returns; wounds and spent Grit remain.

Condition reference

The full condition table follows in the assembled manuscript. A condition's number may mean severity, duration or both. Temporary numbered effects resolve at turn end, then decay by 1. An asterisk prevents automatic decay. Maintained Grappled and binary conditions use their own removal rules.

Use a plausible Main Action to reduce Bleeding, Burning or Freezing by 1 on yourself or an adjacent creature. This is not a universal condition-removal action. Matching resistance applies to Burning and Freezing; Bleeding bypasses it.

Dazed and Grappled restrict category selection at turn start without undoing spent actions. Use the greater restriction when they coexist. Paralyzed, Asleep and Unconscious impose their immediate restrictions. Helpless-state defense Banes apply once when several such states overlap.

Wound reference

The five complete wound tables follow the conditions. They retain all 280 authored results and their recovery values. Use chapter 8 for the wound roll, table choice, applicability fallback and survival procedure. The table's remedy states which lasting effects it removes; immediate displacement and temporary conditions do not recur merely because a scar remains.
